title: Night market
brief: Design the wayfinding and information service for a monthly evening market in a former train yard. Entrance north is step-free, entrance east has stairs, and the west gate is for deliveries until 18:30. Performances move indoors in rain, while most stalls stay outside. The event runs 17:00–21:00, permits only freestanding signs, and has one public address speaker near the stage. Volunteer turnover is high. The organizers can print 24 reusable sign panels and one paper handout; mobile reception is unreliable. Produce a design proposal that a printer, a volunteer lead and an accessibility reviewer can use for the first two market nights.

158529bc9b5e6d0e.text:
# Wayfinding and Information Service: Evening Market at the Train Yard

**Proposal for market nights 1 and 2**

## 1. Design approach

The service has four parts: 24 freestanding sign panels, one paper handout, scripted announcements from the stage speaker, and volunteers with fixed posts and a pocket card. Nothing depends on phones, so there are no QR codes.

Three rules shape everything:

- **Signs carry what stays the same every month.** Panels show no dates, stall names or performer names; anything that varies is written by hand in a wipe-clean box.
- **Every spoken message has a written twin.** The single speaker only reaches people near the stage, so each announcement is also written on the board at the information point.
- **Volunteers need no memory of last month.** Each sign has a letter, a labelled position and a setup photo, and each post has a one-page role card.

## 2. Points to confirm before artwork is final

The proposal makes working assumptions where site facts are not yet known. The volunteer lead should confirm these on a site walk.

| # | To confirm | Working assumption |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Name, location and door of the indoor performance space | Called "the Hall" here; one public door |
| 2 | Whether the Hall door and the toilets are step-free | Unknown; no access symbol is printed until checked |
| 3 | Whether the public may use the west gate after 18:30, and whether it is step-free | Wording works either way (see sign D) |
| 4 | Distance and surface of the outside route from the east entrance to the north entrance | Distance is added to sign B once measured |
| 5 | Lighting at each sign position after dusk | Entrance stands may need clip-on battery lights |
| 6 | Whether chalk or tape position marks are allowed under the permit | If not, rely on setup photos |

## 3. Sign system

### 3.1 Specification for the printer

- **Quantity:** 24 single-sided panels, mounted back to back in 12 weighted A-frame stands (lettered A–L).
- **Size:** A1 portrait (594 × 841 mm), in 5 mm rigid board with a matte anti-glare laminate. Faces marked "write-on" need a dry-wipe laminate.
- **Frames:** these should be solid to the ground with no open crossbar, so a long cane detects them, and weighted against wind.
- **Type:** a sans-serif face in sentence case, never all capitals. Destination names have a minimum 60 mm capital height, secondary lines 30 mm, and nothing is smaller than 15 mm.
- **Colour:** near-black text on a white or pale yellow background. Colour is never the only carrier of meaning; each destination has a word, a symbol and an arrow.
- **Arrows:** these are supplied as removable vinyl decals for nights 1 and 2. Arrow directions depend on final stand positions, which will be adjusted after night 1; permanent arrows are applied after night 2.
- **Labels:** each panel has its letter and face number (for example "F1") printed small at the bottom corner. A label on the back reads "Stand F: [position], this face towards [landmark]".
- **Symbols:** the standard pictograms are step-free access, stairs, toilets, information, stage, covered space and exit.

### 3.2 Panel schedule

| Stand | Position | Face 1 | Face 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | North entrance, just inside | Welcome, site map and "Tonight" box (write-on) | "Exit: north. Step-free." |
| **B** | East entrance, street side, before the stairs | "This entrance has stairs. Step-free entrance: North, [distance], [arrow]" | Same as face 1, for the other street approach |
| **C** | East entrance, market side of the stairs | Welcome, site map and "Tonight" box (write-on) | "Exit: east. Stairs. Step-free exit: North [arrow]" |
| **D** | West gate | Outer: "Deliveries only until 18:30. Vehicles moving. Public entrances: North (step-free), East (stairs)" | Inner: "No public access through this gate before 18:30" |
| **E** | Information point | "Information: ask here", site map, "Tonight" box (write-on) | Same as face 1 |
| **F–I** | Four decision points, set on the site walk | Directional | Directional |
| **J** | Stage | "Stage: tonight's performances" (write-on times) | Directional: Hall, Toilets, Information, Exits |
| **K** | Hall door | "The Hall. Performances are here when it rains." | Directional: Stage, Toilets, Information, Exits |
| **L** | Rain overlays, stored at the information point | "It's raining: performances are now in the Hall [arrow]. Stalls are open outside." | Identical; the two panels slip over both faces of stand J |

**Directional panels (F–I, J2, K2).** Each lists the same destinations in the same order: Stage, the Hall, Toilets, Information, Exit north (step-free), Exit east (stairs). Stage and Hall both appear all the time, so these signs never change with the weather.

**"Tonight" box (A1, C1, E).** This is a wipe-clean panel with two tick boxes, "Performances tonight: ☐ at the Stage ☐ in the Hall (rain)", and three blank lines for start times. It is the only part of the entrance signs that a volunteer edits.

**West gate (D).** The wording is true all evening, so no swap is needed at 18:30. If the organizers open the gate to the public after 18:30, the stand is moved to the side of the gateway. If they do not, it stays in place and a volunteer closes the gate.

**Site map (A1, C1, E, handout).** There is one drawing, used everywhere, and each sign version is rotated so that "up" on the map is straight ahead for the reader.

- It has a "You are here" marker.
- The step-free route from the north entrance to the stage, the Hall, the toilets and the information point is drawn as a bold dashed line.
- Stairs are marked with the stairs symbol.
- Stall areas are shown as zones (for example "Food", "Makers"), not as individual stalls.
- The west gate is labelled "Deliveries until 18:30".

### 3.3 Placement rules

- Stands must leave at least 1.5 m of clear width on every path and must never sit on the step-free route line itself.
- Each stand goes at the decision point, not after it, with the face square to the direction people approach from.
- Stands should go under existing lighting where possible.
- Stand B is the most important sign on site. It must be visible before anyone commits to the stairs, from both directions along the street.

## 4. The handout

The handout is one A4 sheet, double-sided and folded to A5. It is undated so the same print run serves both nights and beyond. Body text is 14 pt minimum, in black on white or pale yellow uncoated paper, so it does not glare and can be written on.

**Side 1 is the map.** It is the same drawing as the signs, with north entrance at the bottom, the step-free route marked and a key that uses words alongside symbols.

**Side 2 has six short blocks:**

1. **Times.** The market is open 17:00–21:00.
2. **Getting in and out.** The north entrance is step-free. The east entrance has stairs. The west gate is for deliveries only until 18:30.
3. **If it rains.** Performances move into the Hall. Most stalls stay open outside.
4. **Finding things.** This covers toilets, the information point and seating, once confirmed.
5. **Announcements.** These are made from the speaker by the stage. If you cannot hear them, the same information is written up at the information point.
6. **Need help?** Volunteers wear [identifier: hi-vis or lanyard colour]. Ask any of them, or go to the information point.

Handouts are given out at the north entrance, the east entrance and the information point. They are offered to every visitor, not left in a pile. Print enough for roughly a third of expected attendance on night 1, then recount the leftovers to set the quantity for night 2.

## 5. Stage speaker announcements

Announcements are read from a laminated script at the stage, slowly, twice each. The information point volunteer writes the same message on the "Tonight" box of stand E at the same time.

| Time | Script |
|---|---|
| 17:00 | "Welcome to the market. We're open until nine. Maps are on the signs at each entrance and at the information point. Volunteers in [identifier] can help you." |
| 18:30 | "Deliveries through the west gate have now finished." If applicable: "The west gate is now open to everyone." |
| On rain | "Because of the rain, performances are moving indoors to the Hall. Follow the signs marked Hall. The stalls are staying open outside." |
| 20:45 | "The market closes in fifteen minutes. The step-free exit is the north entrance. The east exit has stairs." |
| 21:00 | "The market is now closed. Thank you for coming. Please make your way to the exits." |

Performers' start times are announced only if the stage manager wants them. They are always written on stand J and in the "Tonight" boxes.

## 6. Volunteer operation

### 6.1 Posts

There are four posts, each with a role card kept in the sign store.

| Post | Where | Main job |
|---|---|---|
| North | Stand A | Offer handouts; write up the "Tonight" box |
| East | Between stands B and C | Offer handouts; redirect anyone who needs the step-free entrance, and walk with them if they wish |
| Information | Stand E | Answer questions; keep a tally of questions; mirror announcements in writing |
| Rover | Stage, Hall and west gate | Set stand J times; handle the west gate at 18:30; lead the rain switch |

With fewer than four volunteers, the first post to drop is North (stand A does the work), then Rover (the Information post takes those duties). East is never left uncovered while the market is open.

### 6.2 Pocket card

Every volunteer gets a credit-card-sized card, printed with the handouts. It gives the five answers most often needed:

1. The step-free way in and out is the north entrance.
2. The east entrance has stairs.
3. The west gate is for deliveries only until 18:30.
4. When it rains, performances are in the Hall and stalls stay outside.
5. If you don't know, send or walk the person to the information point.

### 6.3 Evening timeline

| Time | Action |
|---|---|
| 16:15 | Place stands A–K using the back labels and setup photos; stand D goes out first. |
| 16:45 | Lead walks the step-free route from north entrance to every destination, checking that it is clear and that signs are lit and legible. Fill in the "Tonight" boxes and stand J. |
| 17:00 | Opening announcement. |
| 18:30 | Rover confirms the last delivery vehicle has left, then moves stand D aside or closes the gate. Announcement. |
| 20:45 | Closing announcement. |
| 21:00 | Collect stands in letter order, wipe the write-on boxes and return the tally sheet to the lead. |

### 6.4 Rain switch

The event lead decides, and no one else does. If rain is forecast, the decision is made by 16:30 and the market opens in rain mode. If rain starts mid-event, the sequence is:

1. The lead tells the stage manager and the Rover.
2. The Rover fits the two L panels over stand J.
3. The rain announcement is made from the stage.
4. The North, East and Information volunteers re-tick their "Tonight" boxes to "in the Hall".
5. The Rover stands at the Hall door for ten minutes to direct people.

Once made, the switch is not reversed that evening, because a second change would confuse more people than it helps.

## 7. Notes for the accessibility reviewer

Please check the following and mark each as accepted, to be changed or to be tested on site.

- **Step-free journey.** Does the dashed route reach every destination, including the Hall and a toilet (items 1–2 in section 2)? Are surfaces such as rails, ballast and cobbles passable for wheels?
- **East entrance.** Is stand B seen early enough, and is the outside route to the north entrance itself step-free, lit and a reasonable distance?
- **Legibility.** Review the type sizes, contrast and glare under the actual evening lighting, and whether pale yellow or white reads better on site.
- **Non-visual access.** There is no tactile or audio map. The fallback is a volunteer who describes the route or walks it with the visitor. Is that adequate for nights 1 and 2?
- **Non-audio access.** Every announcement is mirrored in writing at stand E. Is one location enough?
- **Obstruction.** Review cane detectability of the frames and the 1.5 m clear width.
- **Language.** Review the plain wording, and whether "step-free" and "stairs" are the right terms for this audience.
- **Rain mode.** Does moving indoors change the step-free route or create a pinch point at the Hall door?

## 8. Plan for the first two nights

**Night 1 is a trial.** Arrows are removable decals. The lead photographs each stand in position for the setup sheet. The Information volunteer keeps a tally of questions under five headings: toilets, stage or Hall, entrances and exits, a specific stall, and other. The East volunteer counts how many people are redirected to the north entrance.

**Between the nights.** The lead and the accessibility reviewer meet for 30 minutes with the tallies and photographs. Changes are limited to moving stands, re-pointing arrows, rewording the scripts and adjusting the handout quantity. No panel is reprinted unless the reviewer finds a safety or access fault.

**Night 2 is confirmation.** Volunteers run the same tallies. If the commonest question is the same on both nights, that answer goes on a sign: one of the directional faces is reassigned to it.

**After night 2.** The printer applies permanent arrows. The setup photos, role cards, scripts and pocket card are stored as one laminated pack with the stands.

ad66fea4943e20f3.text:
# Evening Market | Wayfinding and information service

## What visitors need to know before they enter

The market runs from **17:00 to 21:00**. North is the step-free entrance. East has stairs. West is reserved for deliveries until at least 18:30. In rain, performances move indoors and most stalls stay outside. Give visitors these facts where they can still change direction, especially on the east approach, before they have committed to the stairs.

Use the same five destination names on signs, on the handout and in conversation: **North entrance, East entrance, Market stalls, Outdoor stage, Indoor performance room**. Add **Market information** as the fixed meeting and help point just inside North. Keep it staffed from opening until the last visitors leave. A visitor arriving without a phone should be able to find an entrance, reach a destination, learn of a performance move and choose a suitable way out.

## Printer’s schedule | 24 reusable panels

Each numbered face below is one printed panel. Where two messages belong at the same point, fit the panels back to back in one freestanding frame or keep one behind the other for a status change. Print no dates, performer names or timings that vary by month. Bracketed arrows are production instructions. Finalize their direction after walking the site from the visitor’s point of view.

| Panels | Quantity | Principal copy | Placement and use |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 1–2 | 2 | **Market 17:00–21:00** / **Step-free entrance · North [arrow]** | On the two public approaches, before the choice of gates. Put the east approach sign before the first stair. |
| 3 | 1 | **North entrance · Step-free** / Market information inside | Face arriving visitors at North. |
| 4 | 1 | **East entrance · Stairs** / Step-free entrance · North [arrow] | At the last level place where a visitor can turn toward North. |
| 5 | 1 | **Deliveries only** / Public entrance · North [arrow] | Face people approaching West. Keep visible until the gate lead releases the delivery area. |
| 6 | 1 | **West gate open** / Step-free entrance · North [arrow] | Replacement face for panel 5, only if West is approved and opened for visitors. |
| 7 | 1 | **Market information** / Maps and route assistance | At the fixed North information point, readable from the entrance. |
| 8–9 | 2 | **You are here** / Market map | One inside North and one inside East. Give each its own location marker and orient the map to the direction the reader faces. |
| 10–13 | 4 | **Market stalls [arrow]** / **Outdoor stage [arrow]** / **Indoor performance room [arrow]** | Four direction panels for the main junctions. Print only the destinations reached from that particular decision point. |
| 14–16 | 3 | **Step-free exit · North [arrow]** | Face departing visitors at the performance area, stall route and final turn toward North. |
| 17–18 | 2 | **Performances outdoors · Outdoor stage [arrow]** | Dry-weather faces at the information point and the main junction shared by arrivals from East and North. |
| 19–20 | 2 | **Performances indoors · Indoor performance room [arrow]** / Most stalls remain outside | Wet-weather replacements for 17–18 at the same locations. |
| 21 | 1 | **Outdoor stage** | Identify the destination from the audience approach. |
| 22 | 1 | **Performances moved indoors [arrow]** / Most stalls remain outside | At the outdoor stage approach during a move, facing visitors before they enter the audience area. |
| 23 | 1 | **Indoor performance room** | Beside the actual public door, visible along the approach and clear of the door swing. |
| 24 | 1 | **Market exit · East** / Stairs ahead / Step-free exit · North [arrow] | At the last interior choice before the east stairs. |

## Layout, fabrication and placement

Use matte, weather-resistant panels in weighted freestanding frames. A1 portrait is the starting size for approach and junction signs and A2 for door identification. Use a plain sans serif in mixed case, dark lettering on a light ground, generous spacing and one destination per line. Start with a 70 mm capital height for approach headings and 35 mm for supporting directions. Test a full-size proof at the actual decision distance under evening lighting. Enlarge essential words or shorten the copy if readers must walk past the turn to read them. Pair stair and step-free symbols with words. Put arrows beside their own destinations, especially where two routes diverge.

Before authorizing print, the volunteer lead and accessibility reviewer should walk both approaches, the gate-to-gate diversion, routes to both performance venues and the return to North. Mark actual turns, stairs, uneven surfaces, lighting gaps, toilets and public doors on a base plan. Distinguish the verified step-free routes from other pedestrian paths. North’s entrance is confirmed step-free. Any step-free claim beyond it requires checking the whole route, including the indoor threshold and the return journey. If a barrier remains, give its location on both maps and at information so visitors can decide before setting off.

Give every frame a numbered position on the setup plan. Stand it beyond the walking line, with its base detectable by cane and its feet clear of doorways, queues and turning space. Check sightlines from seated and standing positions with stalls trading and people waiting. Keep frames and volunteers outside the west vehicle route. Use existing steady lighting or provide freestanding lighting where the evening check finds a dark sign. Keep official emergency signs and access routes clear throughout.

## One paper handout

Print one two-sided A4 sheet in multiple identical copies for both nights. Offer it unfolded at North and East. Use the first side for a simplified, north-up map with a north arrow, a distinctive outline for the indoor room and street-side landmarks recognizable on arrival. Label both entrances, West gate, Market information, the stalls, the two performance destinations and verified toilets. Draw the checked step-free routes with a thick continuous line and label them directly. Mark stairs at East. Check that all distinctions survive a black-and-white photocopy.

Use the reverse for large, left-aligned text. Lead with the following visitor copy.

> **Evening Market · 17:00–21:00**  
> For step-free entry and exit, use North. East has stairs. Deliveries use West until at least 18:30. Use West only when its sign says “West gate open.”  
> In rain, performances move to the Indoor performance room. Most stalls stay outside. Check the performance sign at Market information or at the main junction for the current location.  
> For directions or a guide, ask at Market information, just inside North. Volunteers at the entrances can also help.

Below this, print short landmark-based directions from East to North and from Market information to the indoor room, using landmarks confirmed on the walk. Set body copy at 16 point or larger and reduce map detail before reducing type. Offer to read the sheet aloud, describe the route or walk with a visitor. Ask which would help and wait for an answer before guiding.

## Volunteer operation on both nights

The duty lead owns the setup plan and records three live facts at Market information: current performance location, West gate status and any route obstruction. Use a pencil log with time and initials. Assign people by post at each shift change: North information, East arrivals, West delivery control, performance contact and a runner. The lead can cover a post during breaks. Keep the runner available for messages between posts because reception is unreliable and the stage speaker reaches only part of the yard.

Brief each incoming volunteer at their post. Show them the nearest numbered sign, the route to North, the indoor door and the person who can confirm a change. Ask them to point the route out and repeat the current performance location. At handover, the outgoing volunteer states the three live facts and stays until the replacement can give directions. For an uncertain answer, use “I’ll check with Market information.” Send the runner while someone stays with the visitor.

**Before 17:00**, inspect the installed signs from both directions, walk the step-free route and clear any encroaching stall stock. Put the current performance faces in view and stage the alternate faces at their change points. Confirm the indoor door is usable before directing anyone there. Give the East volunteer handouts and show them where to intercept visitors before the stairs.

**At 18:30**, the West lead checks for remaining vehicles, outstanding deliveries and a clear public route. If the organizer has approved public use and the area is clear, the duty lead authorizes the face change and sends the runner to update North and East. Otherwise panel 5 stays visible and visitors continue to North. The handout remains accurate if deliveries overrun or West stays closed all evening.

**When rain moves a performance indoors**, the performance contact confirms the room and route are ready and tells the duty lead. The runner coordinates the changes to panels 19, 20 and 22 and briefs East and the stall-area volunteers. The stage contact gives one short announcement and repeats it after a pause: “Performances have moved to the Indoor performance room. Follow the signs from the stage. Most stalls remain outside. A volunteer here can guide you.” Keep a volunteer at the stage approach through the audience move. If admission pauses, station someone at the indoor approach to explain the wait and keep the doorway clear.

**At 21:00**, prioritize outward directions. Keep North information, lighting and exit panels in place until the last visitors have left. Record missing panels, moved frames and any route that became difficult after dark.

## First-night review and second-night acceptance

On night one, the accessibility reviewer should try four journeys: approach East and divert before the stairs, enter North and reach the stalls, find the indoor room from the outdoor stage during a simulated or actual rain move, and return from the room to North after dark. Test the rain message from East with the speaker out of earshot. If the evening stays dry, rehearse the face changes before opening and restore the outdoor faces before admitting visitors.

For each journey, record the first point where the reviewer has to stop, backtrack or ask. At information, volunteers tally repeated questions by location and note the words visitors use for hard-to-find places. Before night two, the lead and reviewer use those observations to reposition frames, revise the spoken directions and assign the runner to any unresolved turn during busy periods. Correct inaccurate printed directions before the affected route opens.

Repeat the four journeys on night two with a newly briefed volunteer. Accept the arrangement when the east diversion is apparent before the stairs, each turn on the verified step-free route is identifiable in evening light, visitors can discover a performance move without hearing the speaker, and each post gives the same current answer about West. Record any remaining barrier, its exact location and the interim direction staff will give.

8a36ce7c71dcc814.text:
# Evening market wayfinding and information proposal

## Visitor routes and operating decisions

The market runs from 17:00 to 21:00. Make the North Entrance the signed step-free arrival route. The East Entrance has stairs, so visitors approaching from the east need directions to North before they reach the staircase. The West Gate serves deliveries until 18:30. Keep it out of the public route on both pilot nights unless the event lead confirms that it can open safely and assigns a volunteer to manage the change. Treat 18:30 as the earliest decision time.

Give the two performance venues distinct names on signs, the handout and the public address system. Use **Outdoor Stage** and **Indoor Performance Hall** throughout. In rain, direct audiences to the hall and tell visitors that most stalls remain outside. Put that information at entrances and inside the yard so everyone can get the update without hearing the speaker or using a phone.

Before artwork goes to print, the event lead and accessibility reviewer should walk the site together. Confirm the outside route from East and West to North, the paths from North to each venue, the location and accessibility of toilets, and the public exit routes. Check surfaces, gradients, thresholds, lighting and any remaining rail grooves or level changes. Walk the routes in both directions and check them again after dark with the market lighting on. Identify a staffed information point on the step-free route just inside North.

Draw arrows from the visitor’s actual approach. If the signed route needs an intermediate turn out of sight of the previous sign, place a sign at that turn. Where a step-free route to a venue or service cannot be verified, print the specific barrier and any verified alternative. Agree with the event lead how visitors will be served if the indoor performance route has an unresolved barrier.

## Print and placement schedule

Print 24 reusable rigid panels for freestanding frames. Each reversible panel counts once. Give each face of a reversible panel the same small setup ID near the bottom edge, with an A or B suffix. The volunteer lead can use the IDs to check each sign and face on the opening walk. Bracketed items below are artwork instructions. Replace them with verified wording or arrows before printing.

| Panels | Printed message and placement |
|---|---|
| 01 | **NORTH ENTRANCE · STEP-FREE · 17:00–21:00**. Face the main approach to North. |
| 02 | **EAST ENTRANCE · STAIRS · STEP-FREE ENTRANCE [arrow] NORTH**. Place before visitors commit to the stairs. |
| 03 | **STEP-FREE ENTRANCE [arrow] NORTH**. Place at the first decision on the outside route from East to North. |
| 04 | **STEP-FREE ENTRANCE [arrow] NORTH**. Place at the next turn or the point where North becomes visible. |
| 05 | Face A **WEST GATE · DELIVERIES ONLY UNTIL 18:30 · PUBLIC ENTRANCE [arrow] NORTH**. Face B **WEST GATE · PUBLIC ENTRANCE [arrow] NORTH**. Keep this upstream of the gate so visitors can divert without entering the delivery area. |
| 06 | Face A **DELIVERY ACCESS ONLY**. Face B **WEST GATE CLOSED TO VISITORS**. Place at the gate. If public opening is approved, remove this panel and deploy 23 and 24 together. |
| 07 | **MARKET INFORMATION · PAPER MAPS**. Place at the staffed information point inside North, visible from the entrance. |
| 08–09 | **STALLS [arrow] · TOILETS [arrow] · PERFORMANCES [arrow]**. Place at the first decision inside North and East, respectively. Point performances toward the first junction with a weather status panel. |
| 10–13 | Face A **PERFORMANCES · OUTDOOR STAGE [arrow]**. Face B **PERFORMANCES MOVED INDOORS · INDOOR PERFORMANCE HALL [arrow] · MOST STALLS STAY OUTSIDE**. Place at North information, inside East, the main performance junction and the approach to the Outdoor Stage, respectively. Use the actual arrow for each face and location. At the Outdoor Stage itself, face A can read **OUTDOOR STAGE · PERFORMANCES HERE**. |
| 14 | **INDOOR PERFORMANCE HALL**. Face arriving visitors at the public doorway. Add verified step-free direction or threshold information if needed. |
| 15–16 | **STALLS [arrow]** and **TOILETS [arrow]**, respectively. Place each where the route branches. Print **STEP-FREE TOILET** with its own arrow if the facility and route are verified and the direction differs. |
| 17–18 | **EXIT [arrow] NORTH · STEP-FREE**. Place at the main yard junction and the indoor hall’s public departure route, respectively. |
| 19 | **EXIT [arrow] EAST · STAIRS**. Place at the decision before the stairs, with the direction to the North exit on the same face. |
| 20–21 | **STEP-FREE ROUTE [arrow]**. Place at the two confirmed turns or surface transitions where the step-free route needs reassurance. Add the destination name where routes diverge. |
| 22 | **ROUTE CLOSED · ASK A VOLUNTEER FOR DIRECTIONS**. Hold at North information for an obstruction. Station a volunteer at the closure while this panel is in use. |
| 23 | Face A **WEST GATE · ENTRANCE TO MARKET**. Face B **WEST GATE · EXIT FROM MARKET**. Use the entrance face toward arriving visitors only after public opening is approved. |
| 24 | **MARKET INFORMATION [arrow] · STEP-FREE EXIT [arrow] NORTH**. Deploy inside West with panel 23 when West opens. |

At an approved West opening, remove panel 05 if it still directs visitors away from the open gate. If West stays closed after 18:30, turn panels 05 and 06 to face B. Keep North and East wayfinding in service until visitors have left. The market panels supplement the venue’s emergency exit signs and procedures.

Use matte, weather-resistant stock and high-contrast lettering, such as near-black on warm white. Make destination names and arrows the largest elements. Start with 75 mm capital height for entrance names and primary directions meant to be read across an approach, and 35 mm for secondary text read nearby. Size panels around the copy and test a full-size proof at the actual decision distance in evening light. Pair standard arrows and access symbols with words. Use color as reinforcement, with the same visual treatment for the step-free route on signs and the map.

Use weighted, stable freestanding frames with flush-fitting panels. Position bases outside the clear walking route, stair landings, door swings and queue paths. Aim sign faces toward approaching visitors and check that people can read them from standing and seated positions. Check for glare, shadows and crowd obstruction at night. Place the gate panels clear of vehicle movements.

## Paper handout

Print one reusable artwork for a two-sided A5 handout. Put **Evening Market · 17:00–21:00** and a large, simplified map on the front. Label North, East, West, Market Information, Stalls, Toilets, Outdoor Stage and Indoor Performance Hall. Mark the verified step-free routes with a bold line keyed in words. Show East’s stairs and the outside approach to North. Label West **Deliveries until 18:30. Check the gate sign for public access.** Include a north arrow and orient the drawing consistently with the site. Keep rail-yard detail only where it helps visitors recognize a landmark.

Use the back for large, plain-text directions that can be read without interpreting the map. Add the verified turns and landmarks after the site walk. Set body copy at 14 pt or larger, with left alignment and generous spacing. Use this copy alongside the route details:

> **Step-free arrival and departure**  
> Use the North Entrance. Market Information is just inside. The East Entrance has stairs.  
>
> **Performances**  
> In dry weather, go to the Outdoor Stage. In rain, performances move to the Indoor Performance Hall and most stalls stay outside. Check the performance signs for tonight’s location.  
>
> **Finding your way**  
> Ask at Market Information for directions, a spoken version of the map or current route information.

Keep copies at North information and give the East volunteer a small supply. Stock West only if it opens. Update visitors verbally when handing out maps during a weather change or route closure. The handout and signs work without mobile reception.

## Volunteer running order

Assign named owners at the pre-opening briefing. The **event lead** decides weather status, route closures and West Gate access. The **information volunteer** stays at North. The **route volunteer** checks East and the yard junction and helps redirect visitors. The **stage volunteer** checks both venues with the event lead and makes the announcement. Assign gate coverage whenever deliveries, a West opening or an active diversion require it. If staffing is short, keep West closed to visitors and prioritize North information, the East diversion and the performance junction.

**Before 17:00.** Walk the outside approach, both public entrances, the stall and toilet routes, and both performance routes. Check the panel IDs, arrows, current performance faces and lighting. Give each volunteer a handout. Ask each person to point out the step-free entrance, explain where performances go in rain and say what they will tell someone arriving at West. Agree who covers North if its volunteer needs to leave.

**When performances move indoors.** The event lead confirms that the hall and public route are ready. The stage volunteer covers the Outdoor Stage approach while the route and information volunteers turn panels 10–13 and verify the arrows. Relay the change face to face if phones are unreliable. Once the signs and staff are in place, announce near the stage, “Performances have moved to the Indoor Performance Hall. Follow the performance signs. Most stalls are still outside. For help with the route, ask a volunteer.” Repeat for visitors gathering at the former stage. If the hall reaches capacity, station a volunteer at the last junction before the hall queue to tell arrivals what to expect and keep the route clear.

**At 18:30.** Confirm that deliveries have finished and check for moving vehicles, barriers and route conflicts. If West stays closed, turn 05 and 06. If the event lead approves public opening, position the gate volunteer and set 23 and 24 before admitting visitors. Update North information in person.

**At 21:00.** Keep exit signs and lighting available while visitors leave. Direct anyone seeking a step-free exit to North using the verified route. Collect the panels after the public areas clear and record damage or placement changes.

## First two market nights

On night one, observe the first arrival rush, the West Gate changeover and departure. If the weather stays dry, rehearse the rain change before opening, then reset the signs to the announced location. Ask the accessibility reviewer to follow the route from the East approach to North, then to the toilets, stalls, both performance venues and back to North. Record where visitors backtrack, miss an arrow, encounter a blocked path or receive conflicting directions. Note the panel ID and the direction they approached from.

Before night two, adjust frame positions, volunteer posts and briefing instructions using those observations. Verify every moved sign from the visitor’s approach and compare the handout with the revised placement. Escalate wrong printed arrows, inaccessible routes and misleading access claims to the event lead before opening. Cover incorrect directions and staff the affected decision point until corrected artwork or a verified route is in place. Repeat the night-one checks with a volunteer new to the setup. Judge the pilot by whether visitors can find North before reaching the stairs, reach the current performance venue without relying on the announcement, understand West Gate’s status and follow a clear step-free route out after dark.
